# The panel's HTTP API

What `kleidos-meter serve` answers, route by route. This page is written by `scripts/gen_http_api_doc.py` from the schema the panel itself serves at `GET /api/schema`; a test fails when the two differ. How to start the panel, use it and stop it, with worked examples, is in [panel.md](panel.md).

## Conventions

The address is `http://127.0.0.1:8040/` unless serve was told another (`--bind`, `--http`). It is unauthenticated and listens on the loopback only. Every answer is one JSON object but the event stream and an export.

- **A change is a POST with `X-Kleidos-Meter: 1`.** A GET never changes the instrument.
- **The `Host` must name the loopback** (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`), and no answer approves another origin.
- **A report is an object of its own keys.** A canonical integer is a JSON integer in the unit its key names (`i_na`, `vbus_uv`, `hold_s`), `-` is `null`, anything else is the instrument's text, and so are an integer beyond 2^53 and the keys `cal_date`, `cal_tag`, `chip`, `die`, `elf`, `fw`, `image`, `mfg`, `model`, `rev`, `serial`.
- **`errors`** are what the instrument queued for that message, oldest first, each `{code, text}`. What it queues on its own (a hold's release, `113` to `115`, relays a reset released, `116`, and a message an overrun discarded, `-363`) is never a reply's: whichever message drains it, it goes to `/api/events` as an `error` of kind `device`, and to the running capture's `meta.json`.
- **A message** is at most 255 bytes with the `;:SYST:ERR:ALL?` serve adds to it, printable ASCII, every quote it opens closed (the error query after an open one would be quoted and get no answer).
- **While a sequence runs** every change answers 409 (`sequence_running`) but `POST /api/abort`, `POST /api/sequences/answer` and `POST /api/sequences/abort`.
- **While a pin map is applied and checked** every change answers 409 (`pins_changing`) but `POST /api/abort`.
- **While another controller holds the line** every route that talks to the instrument answers 423; the ones that say so below do not.

A refusal's body holds `error`, a short word, and `detail`, a sentence.

| Status | Says |
|---|---|
| 200 | done; the body is what the route answers |
| 400 | the request is malformed, or refused before anything was sent (a value of the wrong form, a message the instrument would discard, a GET that would act); or the instrument queued a command error (`-1xx`) |
| 403 | a change without `X-Kleidos-Meter: 1` (`header_missing`), or from a page of another origin (`foreign_origin`) |
| 404 | no such route, relay order, sequence or run |
| 405 | the route does not take the method; a GET never changes the instrument |
| 409 | the instrument refused it (an execution or device error: `-2xx`, `-3xx`, `100` and up, in `errors`), or serve did: a capture or a sequence runs, a window serve did not open is open, a pin map is being applied, a relay is not at rest, there is nothing to stop |
| 411, 413 | the body has no `Content-Length`, or is longer than 16384 bytes |
| 421 | the `Host` header does not name the loopback |
| 423 | another controller holds the line: `holder` names it |
| 500 | a bug of serve's own, in its log |
| 502 | the instrument answered something other than what was asked |
| 503 | 32 requests run already, the queue of messages is full, the line is down (`Retry-After` says when to come back) or serve is stopping |
| 504 | the answer did not come in time |

|---|---|---|---|
| [`GET /api/schema`](#get-apischema) | no | no | this schema |
| [`GET /api/status`](#get-apistatus) | no | no | the line, the executor and the last status poll; sends nothing |
| [`GET /api/health`](#get-apihealth) | no | yes | health, heap, watchdog, identity and calibration reports |
| [`GET /api/query`](#get-apiquery) | no | yes | queries that read without acting, as JSON |
| [`POST /api/scpi`](#post-apiscpi) | yes | yes | program messages, one per line, each with its errors |
| [`GET /api/settings`](#get-apisettings) | no | yes | every setting as the instrument answers it, and each range's shunt with its uncertainty |

| [`GET /api/settings/shunt/preview`](#get-apisettingsshuntpreview) | no | yes | what an override would write, against the registry's figure |
| [`POST /api/settings/shunt`](#post-apisettingsshunt) | yes | yes | an override with its uncertainty and confirm: true, written and kept on the host |
| [`GET /api/calibration`](#get-apicalibration) | no | yes | the registry's verdict on the instrument |
| [`POST /api/calibration/restore`](#post-apicalibrationrestore) | yes | yes | the registry's working copy written back (the revert), the host's overrides removed |
| [`GET /api/sequences`](#get-apisequences) | no | no | the sequence running or the last one |

| [`POST /api/sequences/abort`](#post-apisequencesabort) | yes | no | the running sequence aborted: its wait ends, its cleanup runs |

### `GET /api/schema`

This schema.

Answers the settings, profiles, relay orders, sequences and routes declared here, `mutation_header`, `clearing_queries`, `pin_orders` (what they change outlives serve) and `text_keys`.

### `GET /api/status`

The line, the executor and the last status poll; sends nothing.

Answers `link`, `polling`, `in_flight`, `queued`, `held` (who holds the line, or null), `passthrough` (its URL, its client and the last one's outcome), `status` and `health` (the last poll's reports), `instrument`, `foreign_window` (a window serve did not open), `reboots`, `capture` and `live`.

### `GET /api/health`

Health, heap, watchdog, identity and calibration reports.

Answers one report a key (`health`, `heap`, `watchdog`, `info`, `calibration`), and `local_elf`: the local build's `elf` against the instrument's, `matches` null when either has none; its `path` is relative to serve's working directory or the repository, else the build's last two components: never an absolute path.

Sends `SYST:HEAL?`, `DIAG:HEAP?`, `DIAG:WATC?`, `SYST:INF?`, `CAL:DATA?`.

### `GET /api/query`

Queries that read without acting, as JSON.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `q` | query | yes | one message of queries |

Answers `message`, `units` (each answer as the instrument wrote it), `fields` (each report as an object, `{}` for an answer that is none), `errors`, `elapsed_s`.

### `POST /api/scpi`

Program messages, one per line, each with its errors.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `body` | text body | yes | program messages, one per line, never a ring dump |

Answers `replies`, one a message: `message`, `units`, `errors`, `elapsed_s`. It is a transport: 200 whatever the instrument queued. The messages run in order; when one after the first fails (a time-out, a full queue, the line down or handed over), the answer is still 200, with the `replies` of those that ran, `failed` (`message`, `error`, `detail`) and `unsent`, the messages never sent, and no `Retry-After`: the ones that ran have changed the instrument.

### `GET /api/settings`

Every setting as the instrument answers it, and each range's shunt with its uncertainty.

Answers `settings` (each as its query answers it, text), and `shunt`: the registry's `verdict`, `quotable`, the `banner`, and for each of the two `ranges` the value it converts with, its `source`, its `uncertainty`, the `registry`'s figures, the `deviation_ppm` and the `override`.

Sends `*IDN?`, `SYST:INF?`, `CAL:DATA?`.

### `POST /api/settings`

Settings written, then read back from the instrument.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<setting>` | JSON body | no | a value of the form its setting takes, one or more settings |

Answers `written` (the units sent, in the settings' order), `errors`, and `settings`: what was written, read back (a profile reads its channels and its averaging back too).

### `GET /api/settings/shunt/preview`

What an override would write, against the registry's figure.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `range` | query | yes | 0 or 1 |
| `ohms` | query | no | ohms (the value, once: `ohms` or `uohm`) |
| `uohm` | query | no | micro-ohms (the value, once: `ohms` or `uohm`) |
| `expanded_ppm` | query | no | `U` at `k = 2`, ppm (its uncertainty, exactly one of the four) |
| `expanded_uohm` | query | no | `U` at `k = 2`, micro-ohms (its uncertainty, exactly one of the four) |
| `tolerance_ppm` | query | no | a rectangular limit, ppm (its uncertainty, exactly one of the four) |
| `tolerance_uohm` | query | no | a rectangular limit, micro-ohms (its uncertainty, exactly one of the four) |
| `note` | query | no | where the figures come from, printable ASCII, at most 200 |

Answers `unit` (what would be sent), `uncertainty`, `device_uohm`, `registry`, `deviation_ppm`, `normalized_error`, `quotable` and `banner`.

Sends `*IDN?`, `SYST:INF?`, `CAL:DATA?`.

### `POST /api/settings/shunt`

An override with its uncertainty and confirm: true, written and kept on the host.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `range` | JSON body | yes | 0 or 1 |
| `ohms` | JSON body | no | ohms (the value, once: `ohms` or `uohm`) |
| `uohm` | JSON body | no | micro-ohms (the value, once: `ohms` or `uohm`) |
| `expanded_ppm` | JSON body | no | `U` at `k = 2`, ppm (its uncertainty, exactly one of the four) |
| `expanded_uohm` | JSON body | no | `U` at `k = 2`, micro-ohms (its uncertainty, exactly one of the four) |
| `tolerance_ppm` | JSON body | no | a rectangular limit, ppm (its uncertainty, exactly one of the four) |
| `tolerance_uohm` | JSON body | no | a rectangular limit, micro-ohms (its uncertainty, exactly one of the four) |
| `note` | JSON body | no | where the figures come from, printable ASCII, at most 200 |
| `confirm` | JSON body | yes | `true` |

Answers `written` (the unit sent), the `override` kept, and `shunt` after it.

Sends `*IDN?`, `SYST:INF?`, `CAL:DATA?`, `SENS:CURR:SHUN:RANG1`.

### `GET /api/calibration`

The registry's verdict on the instrument.

Answers `verdict`: `status` (`applied` is the one to measure on), `ok`, `serial`, `event`, `differences`, `warnings` and its `lines`; and `registry_problem`.

Sends `*IDN?`, `SYST:INF?`, `CAL:DATA?`.

### `POST /api/calibration/restore`

The registry's working copy written back (the revert), the host's overrides removed.

Answers the verdicts `before` and `after`, whether anything was `written`, what it `said`, `cleared_override`; 409 when the registry has no copy for the instrument.

Sends `*IDN?`, `SYST:INF?`, `CAL:DATA?`, `SENS:CURR:SHUN`, `SENS:CURR:SHUN:RANG1`, `CAL:TAG`, `CAL:DATE`, `CAL:VBUS`.

### `GET /api/sequences`

The sequence running or the last one.

Answers `state` (`idle`, `running`, `prompt`, `cleanup`), `sequence`, `number`, `params`, `outcome` and `detail` once it ended, `prompt` (`id`, `text`, `choices`) while it asks, `total` and the `steps` begun, the `cleanup`'s, the `results` kept, the `run` of its capture, `elapsed_s`.

### `POST /api/sequences/run`

One sequence started, its steps as data, its cleanup always run.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | JSON body | yes | the sequence's name |
| `params` | JSON body | no | an object of its parameters, each an integer |

Answers the same as `GET /api/sequences`, as the sequence began.

### `POST /api/sequences/answer`

The running sequence's question answered.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | JSON body | yes | the question's `id` |
| `answer` | JSON body | yes | one of its `choices` |

Answers the same as `GET /api/sequences`.

### `POST /api/sequences/abort`

The running sequence aborted: its wait ends, its cleanup runs.

Answers the same as `GET /api/sequences`; 409 when none runs.

### `GET /api/relays`

ROUTe:STATe? and ROUTe:RESult?, the circuit and the last order.

Answers `result` and `state`, the two reports.

Sends `ROUT:RES?`, `ROUT:STAT?`.

### `POST /api/relays/{relay}`

One relay order, with only the flags given, its result and the circuit after it.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `relay` | path | yes | a relay order's name |
| `state` | JSON body | no | a word of its choices; an order with none takes `ms` |
| `ms` | JSON body | no | a duration, milliseconds, for an order with no choices |
| `force` | JSON body | no | `true` adds `FORCe` |
| `live` | JSON body | no | `true` adds `LIVE` |

Answers `order` (the unit sent), `errors`, and the `result` and `state` after it.

Sends `ROUT:RES?`, `ROUT:STAT?`.

### `GET /api/pins`

The board's pins, the live pin map, the staged one and the last change's result.

Answers `board` (the package's pin table: every terminal, its class and its reason, the roles and the defaults), `table` (`package` and `instrument`, the table's digest on each side, and whether it `matches`: when it does not, staging and applying are refused), `live`, `pending` and `result` (the instrument's reports) and `differs` (the fields staged otherwise than they run).

Sends `SYST:PINS?`, `SYST:PINS:PEND?`, `SYST:PINS:RES?`.

### `POST /api/pins/stage`

Fields of the pin map staged and judged; nothing on the board changes.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<field>` | JSON body | no | a field of the map, one or more: a role's GPIO or `null`, a pull (`up`, `off`), a relay's active level (`high`, `low`), `addr` (`auto` or a number), `scl_hz` |
| `clear` | JSON body | no | `true` starts from the live map, the staged one dropped |

Answers `sent` (the units), `errors` and `pending`, the staged map with its verdict (`valid`, and when 0 the `problem` and the field it is `at`).

Sends `SYST:PINS?`, `SYST:PINS:PEND?`, `SYST:PINS:STAG`, `SYST:PINS:ADDR`, `SYST:PINS:CLOC`, `SYST:PINS:CLE`.

### `POST /api/pins/apply`

The staged map made the live one: proved on the board and kept, or reverted.

Answers `order` (the unit sent), `errors`, `result` (the instrument's report of it: `ok`, or `reverted` with the last good map back, 409), `live` and `pending` after it, and `check`, null unless a relay moved: the null-path check made on its new pad, `passed` (the live map then reads `verified` 1), its `errors`, its `result`, the circuit's `state` and a `detail`. Refused unsent while a sequence (409 `sequence_running`) or a capture (409 `capture_running`, `window_open`) runs, while another controller holds the line (423 `held`) and while a relay is not at rest (409 `relays_not_at_rest`, with the `state`); 409 `table_differs` when the instrument's table is another.

Sends `SYST:PINS?`, `SYST:PINS:PEND?`, `SYST:PINS:RES?`, `ROUT:RES?`, `ROUT:STAT?`, `ROUT:NULL ON`, `ROUT:NULL OFF`, `SYST:COMM:I2C:FREQ?`, `SYST:PINS:APPL`.

### `POST /api/pins/defaults`

The rig's own pin map back, with the same checks; it needs no INA228.

Answers `order` (the unit sent), `errors`, `result` (the instrument's report of it: `ok`, or `reverted` with the last good map back, 409), `live` and `pending` after it, and `check`, null unless a relay moved: the null-path check made on its new pad, `passed` (the live map then reads `verified` 1), its `errors`, its `result`, the circuit's `state` and a `detail`. Refused unsent while a sequence (409 `sequence_running`) or a capture (409 `capture_running`, `window_open`) runs, while another controller holds the line (423 `held`) and while a relay is not at rest (409 `relays_not_at_rest`, with the `state`).

Sends `SYST:PINS?`, `SYST:PINS:PEND?`, `SYST:PINS:RES?`, `ROUT:RES?`, `ROUT:STAT?`, `ROUT:NULL ON`, `ROUT:NULL OFF`, `SYST:COMM:I2C:FREQ?`, `SYST:PINS:DEF`.

### `POST /api/abort`

ABORt, ahead of the queue under an acquisition; a running sequence is aborted too.

Answers `sent`, the message's reply, and `sequence` (the one aborted, or null).

Sends `ABOR`.

### `GET /api/events`

Server-Sent Events: samples, marks, status, errors, sequences and the ring.

Answers an event stream, resumed after the `Last-Event-ID` header when it is sent; 503 while eight others are open.

| Event | Carries |
|---|---|
| `samples` | every 100 ms, the samples since the last batch as columns of integers: `n0` (the first row's index in the capture), `count`, `t_us`, and `i_na`, `v_uv`, `p_uw`, `die_mc` of the channels it holds, `null` in a row that lacks one |
| `mark` | a mark record in its place among the batches: `label`, `n`, `t_us` |
| `status` | `kind`: `hello` (the first event of a stream), `poll` (the last status poll), `link`, `reboot`, `capture`, `passthrough`, `settings` (`changed`: the settings a message that was written changes, whoever sent it) |
| `error` | `kind`: `device` (errors nobody asked for), `overflow` (a line too long to hold), `recorder` (a run's files could not be written) |
| `sequence` | the sequence's state, as `GET /api/sequences` answers it, at each change |
| `ring` | a ring capture's fill (`samples`, `running`) and its dump's progress (`dump`) |
| `lost` | to one stream only: the `events` it missed, and the `samples` among them, `null` when unknown |

An event's id is `<epoch>-<seq>-<rows>`. A browser that reconnects with `Last-Event-ID` goes on right after it, or is told with `lost` what it missed.

### `GET /api/capture`

The recorder: the capture serve owns, or the last one.

Answers `state` (`idle`, `starting`, `running`, `stopping`), `run`, `data_dir` (relative to serve's working directory or the repository, else its last two components: never an absolute path), and `profile`, `seconds`, `elapsed_s`, `samples`, `marks` and `noise_reduction` (the INA228's averaging, null until the capture has started) of the capture; `last`: the last run's summary.

### `POST /api/capture/start`

A capture configured, started and recorded into a run.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `profile` | JSON body | yes | a profile's name, long or short |
| `channels` | JSON body | no | a list of `CURR`, `VOLT`, `POW`, `TEMP`, or `DEFault`; the instrument's as they stand when absent |
| `seconds` | JSON body | no | stop it after so long, at most 604800 (a week); until it is stopped when absent |
| `label` | JSON body | no | a note kept in the run, printable ASCII, at most 80 |

Answers `state` (`idle`, `starting`, `running`, `stopping`), `run`, `data_dir` (relative to serve's working directory or the repository, else its last two components: never an absolute path), and `profile`, `seconds`, `elapsed_s`, `samples`, `marks` and `noise_reduction` (the INA228's averaging, null until the capture has started) of the capture, as it began.

Sends `SENS:PROF`, `SENS:FUNC:ON`, `SENS:FUNC:ON:DEF`, `INIT`, `FETC:HEAD?`.

### `POST /api/capture/stop`

The capture closed, its statistics and its ring read, its run finished.

Answers `run`, its `summary` and its `meta` (`meta.json`).

Sends `ABOR`, `FETC:STAT?`, `FETC:HEAD?`, `TRAC:POIN?`, `TRAC:DATA?`.

### `POST /api/capture/mark`

A mark in the running capture.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | JSON body | yes | 1 to 15 printable characters, no space and none of `,` `;` `=` `"` `'` |

Answers `label` and the instrument's `errors`.

Sends `TRAC:MARK`.

### `GET /api/runs`

The recorded runs, newest first.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | query | no | how many, 1 to 1000 (100) |

Answers `runs`, a summary each: `id`, `state`, `complete`, `profile`, `format`, `label`, `started`, `ended`, `ended_by`, `samples`, `dropped`, `stream_samples`, `marks`, `trace`, `noise_reduction` (the INA228's averaging, as `meta.json` has it: its `state`, `on` or `off`, the `count`, `conversion_us` and `period_us`; null when unknown), and `recording` (true for the run serve is still writing).

### `GET /api/runs/{run}`

A run's meta.json.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | path | yes | the run's id, as `GET /api/runs` lists it |

Answers the run's `meta.json`.

### `GET /api/runs/{run}/export`

A run's records as a download.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | path | yes | the run's id, as `GET /api/runs` lists it |
| `format` | query | no | `text`, `csv` or `json` (`csv`) |

Answers the file, named `<run>.txt`, `<run>.csv` or `<run>.json`; 409 (`recording`) while the run is still being written, since an export is made once and kept.

### `GET /api/runs/{run}/decimated`

A run's count, mean, root mean square, minimum and maximum per bucket, for a chart.

| Takes | In the | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | path | yes | the run's id, as `GET /api/runs` lists it |
| `column` | query | no | `i_na`, `v_uv`, `p_uw` or `die_mc` (`i_na`) |
| `buckets` | query | no | how many buckets of equal duration, 1 to 10000 (1000) |
| `t0_us` | query | no | the first timestamp (the run's) |
| `t1_us` | query | no | the last timestamp (the run's) |

Answers `column`, `t0_us`, `t1_us`, `bucket_us`, and the columns `t_us` (each bucket's start), `min`, `max`, `n` (its samples), `mean` (their arithmetic mean) and `rms` (their root mean square) of the buckets that hold samples.

## Settings

What `GET /api/settings` reads and `POST /api/settings` writes, in the order they are written. A value is checked for its form, never for its range: that is the instrument's to refuse. The flags are the instrument's ([scpi.md](scpi.md)): `D` needs the INA228, `R` is refused while a capture or a null window runs, `C` also until one that ended by itself is closed.

| Setting | Value | Written with | Flags | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `i2c_hz` | an integer, Hz | `SYSTem:COMMunicate:I2C:FREQuency` | `DR` | the INA228 bus, 50000..1000000 Hz; BURST needs 1000000 |
| `profile` | one of `TRACe`, `STATe`, `SLEep`, `BURSt` | `SENSe:PROFile` | `DRC` | the sampling profile; resets the channels to its default |
| `channels` | a list of `CURR`, `VOLT`, `POW`, `TEMP`, or `DEFault` | `SENSe:FUNCtion:ON` | `R` | what a capture streams; none on a ring profile |
| `range` | one of `0`, `1` | `SENSe:CURRent:RANGe:INDex` | `DRC` | ADCRANGE: 0 is ±163.84 mV (1.6384 A), 1 is ±40.96 mV (0.4096 A) |
| `capture` | one of `DATA`, `STATistics` | `SENSe:CAPTure` | `R` | DATA streams or fills the ring; STATistics keeps the statistics only |
| `limit` | `true` or `false` | `SENSe:CAPTure:LIMit` | `R` | ON ends a capture by itself after the sample count |
| `threshold` | a number, or `OFF`, A | `SENSe:CURRent:THReshold` | `R` | a level the next captures count against, or OFF |
| `hysteresis` | a number, A | `SENSe:CURRent:THReshold:HYSTeresis` | `R` | how far below the level the count falls back |
| `threshold_marks` | `true` or `false` | `SENSe:CURRent:THReshold:MARK` | `R` | ON marks each crossing of the threshold in a streamed capture |
| `sample_count` | an integer | `SAMPle:COUNt` | `R` | samples one acquisition takes, and the limit's count |
| `trigger_source` | one of `IMMediate`, `LEVel` | `TRIGger:SOURce` | `R` | what starts a ring capture's record |
| `trigger_level` | a number, A | `TRIGger:LEVel` | `R` | the current a level trigger fires at |
| `trigger_slope` | one of `POSitive`, `NEGative` | `TRIGger:SLOPe` | `R` | upwards or downwards through the level |
| `pretrigger` | an integer | `TRIGger:PRETrigger` | `R` | samples kept from before the crossing |
| `average_count` | one of `1`, `4`, `16`, `64`, `128`, `256`, `512`, `1024` | `SENSe:AVERage:COUNt` | `DRC` | conversions averaged into one sample of the live profile, with averaging ON |
| `average_aperture` | a number, s: one of `0.00005`, `0.000084`, `0.00015`, `0.00028`, `0.00054`, `0.001052`, `0.002074`, `0.00412` | `SENSe:CURRent:APERture` | `DRC` | the time one conversion of the shunt takes on the live profile, with averaging ON |
| `average` | `true` or `false` | `SENSe:AVERage[:STATe]` | `DRC` | changes the live profile's measurement: ON converts with the count and the time above instead of its own; OFF at every boot, refused on BURST |
| `format` | read only | `FORMat[:DATA]` | `R` | the stream record format, shown; serve never changes it |

## Profiles

| Profile | A sample every | Goes to | Channels by default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TRACe` | 280 µs | the ring | – |
| `STATe` | 1152 µs | the stream | `CURR` |
| `SLEep` | 67520 µs | the stream | `CURR`, `VOLT`, `TEMP` |
| `BURSt` | 100 µs | the ring | – |

## Relay orders

The `{relay}` of `POST /api/relays/{relay}`. A flag goes out only when the request sets it.

| Order | Takes | Flags | Sends | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lead` | `state`: `OPEN`, `CLOSe` | `FORCe`, `LIVE` | `ROUTe:LEAD` | Relay 1, the DUT's battery lead: OPEN leaves the DUT without its battery: FORCe is required |
| `lead_cycle` | `ms` | `FORCe`, `LIVE` | `ROUTe:LEAD:CYCLe` | Relay 1 opened and reclosed: Relay 1 held open for 1..60000 ms from path=shunt; FORCe is required |
| `bypass` | `state`: `ON`, `OFF` | `FORCe`, `LIVE` | `ROUTe:BYPass` | Relay 2, the bypass across the shunt: ON takes the shunt off the DUT's current: FORCe under a capture |
| `nullpath` | `state`: `ON`, `OFF` | `LIVE`, `FORCe` | `ROUTe:NULLpath` | The null path (Relay 2 then Relay 1): ON closes Relay 2 and opens Relay 1, make-before-break, checking each step |
| `relay3` | `state`: `ON`, `OFF` | `LIVE` | `ROUTe:RELay#` | Relay 3, spare: not wired on the rig: the instrument refuses the order |
| `relay4` | `state`: `ON`, `OFF` | `LIVE` | `ROUTe:RELay#` | Relay 4, spare: not wired on the rig: the instrument refuses the order |

## Sequences

The `name` and `params` of `POST /api/sequences/run`. What each one moves is in [panel.md](panel.md#what-each-sequence-moves).

| Sequence | Parameters | What it does | Sends |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HEALTH` | – | identity, reset reason, stacks, heap counts, watchdog, self-test and bus scan | `*IDN?`, `SYST:INF?`, `SYST:HEAL?`, `DIAG:HEAP?`, `DIAG:WATC?`, `*TST?`, `DIAG:I2C:SCAN?` |
| `NULL_RELAY` | `seconds`: 1 to 600 s (5) | a null with the DUT on the bypass (Relay 2 then Relay 1), the path released after | `ROUT:NULL`, `ROUT:STAT?`, `CAL:ZERO`, `SYST:STAT?`, `ABOR`, `CAL:ZERO:RES?` |
| `NULL_LEAD` | `seconds`: 1 to 600 s (5) | a null with Relay 1 open (FORCe: the DUT has no battery), the lead reclosed after | `ROUT:LEAD`, `ROUT:STAT?`, `CAL:ZERO`, `SYST:STAT?`, `ABOR`, `CAL:ZERO:RES?`, `ROUT:NULL` |
| `STATE` | `seconds`: 1 to 3600 s (10) | a streamed capture of a state: bus, shunt and temperature at 1152 us | `SENS:PROF`, `INIT`, `FETC:HEAD?`, `ABOR`, `FETC:STAT?` |
| `SLEEP` | `seconds`: 1 to 86400 s (60) | a streamed capture of deep sleep, averaged 16 at 67.52 ms | `SENS:PROF`, `INIT`, `FETC:HEAD?`, `ABOR`, `FETC:STAT?` |
| `TRACE` | – | a ring of 1048576 shunt samples at 280 us, then its dump | `SENS:PROF`, `INIT`, `FETC:HEAD?`, `ABOR`, `FETC:STAT?`, `TRAC:POIN?`, `TRAC:DATA?` |
| `BURST` | – | a ring at 100 us on a 1 MHz bus, then its dump and the bus's clock back | `SYST:COMM:I2C:FREQ?`, `SYST:COMM:I2C:FREQ`, `SENS:PROF`, `INIT`, `FETC:HEAD?`, `ABOR`, `FETC:STAT?`, `TRAC:POIN?`, `TRAC:DATA?` |
| `COLD_BOOT` | `off_ms`: 1 to 60000 ms (2000); `seconds`: 1 to 600 s (10) | the DUT's boot from power-off: a capture across a lead cycle, its moves marked | `SENS:PROF`, `INIT`, `FETC:HEAD?`, `TRAC:MARK`, `ROUT:LEAD:CYCL`, `ROUT:STAT?`, `ABOR`, `FETC:STAT?`, `ROUT:NULL` |
| `CAL_VERIFY` | – | the instrument's calibration against the registry's copy | `*IDN?`, `SYST:INF?`, `CAL:DATA?` |
| `CAL_RESTORE` | – | the registry's copy written back where it differs, then verified | `*IDN?`, `SYST:INF?`, `CAL:DATA?`, `SENS:CURR:SHUN`, `SENS:CURR:SHUN:RANG1`, `CAL:TAG`, `CAL:DATE`, `CAL:VBUS` |

## What a GET never asks

`GET /api/query` takes only queries that read without acting. It refuses a command, a query the `R` flag marks, a header the instrument does not have, and the queries whose reading clears what they read: `*ESR?`, `STATus:OPERation[:EVENt]?`, `STATus:QUEStionable[:EVENt]?`, `SYSTem:ERRor:ALL?`, `SYSTem:ERRor[:NEXT]?`. `POST /api/scpi` takes them all but a ring dump, which the recorder fetches to a file.
